subject: Resilience thresholds and remedy scaling proposal for EdgeWare
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@edgeware.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Resilience thresholds and remedy scaling — initial proposal

Hi Sanjay,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Following up with a concrete framing that we think balances EdgeWare's need for predictable remediation economics with Redwood's operational model across regional workloads. Attaching a short PDF (SLA_Remedy_Scaling_v1.pdf) that lays this out visually. Key points below: 

1) Baseline availability: Redwood proposes a 99.95% monthly availability target for the global service. For regionally scoped commitments (e.g., us-west), we can offer a region-level target of 99.9% by mutual agreement.

2) Remedy scaling (monthly): instead of a single flat credit, we propose a sliding remedy ladder tied to the monthly regional availability:
   - 99.9% — 99.7%: 0.5% invoice credit
   - 99.7% — 99.0%: 2.0% invoice credit
   - <99.0%: 6.0% invoice credit (capped at 6% for that month)

   This structure keeps remedies proportionate to impact and avoids large one-off swings for marginal drops.

3) Latency SLOs: for bursty query patterns in us-west you asked about a looser p99 target. We can add a regional p99 latency target with a separate, smaller remedy band tied to p99 exceedances (remedy accrues only if both availability and latency drop below thresholds in the same month).

4) Maintenance & planned work: standard 4-hour maintenance windows will be excluded; planned windows will be communicated 7 days in advance for anything >30 minutes. Emergency maintenance invoked for security will be communicated as soon as possible and excluded.

5) Operational mitigations: we will include an automatic fallback to a compatible lower-capacity variant in the region before applying credits (where feasible), and a monthly postmortem summary for any month with a remedy.

Next steps: 1) I attached a short workbook that maps example invoices to remedies; 2) If this framing is acceptable, we'd like procurement to confirm whether they prefer direct invoice credits vs. an escrow/holdback mechanism.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman

Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Resilience thresholds and remedy scaling — initial proposal

Naomi —

Thanks for the clear layout. A few items from procurement and platform: 

- Procurement asks whether remedies can be split into two mechanisms: a modest invoice credit + a contractual holdback that accumulates and is reconciled quarterly. They want the option in case capturing credits conflicts with our internal billing cadence.

- On regional p99: we operate traffic spikes from real-time bidding and are sensitive to even short-lived p99 excursions. Can you confirm the p99 band and whether remedies would be triggered on short bursts or sustained exceedances (e.g., >=5 minutes)? We want to avoid per-minute credit churning.

- Also curious whether Redwood would accept a 14-day cure period before remedies kick in — procurement wants a window for remediation and operational mitigations to be applied and measured.

If possible, please loop your legal/finance so we can get a rough path to contract language.

Best,
Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform, EdgeWare
sanjay@edgeware.ai
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@edgeware.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Resilience thresholds and remedy scaling — initial proposal

Sanjay — thanks for the quick feedback. Looping Ben (sales ops), Marissa (product/reliability), and Laura (legal) to align on two fronts: billing mechanism and cure windows. Quick answers and a revised proposal below. Updated PDF attached (SLA_Remedy_Scaling_v1.pdf — revision notes on page 2).

1) Holdback vs. direct credit: we can support either. Proposed default is direct invoice credit (simpler operationally). If EdgeWare prefers holdback, Redwood will accept a quarterly reconciliation model where unclaimed remedies are applied as a one-time adjustment. We'll record the election in the contract exhibit.

2) Trigger definition for latency remedies: Marissa suggests remedies for p99 should be measured as a rolling 60-minute window aggregated at 1-minute granularity and only accrue if the 60-minute window median of per-minute p99s exceeds the target for at least one 10-minute contiguous period. In short: prevents minute-scale flaps from creating credits while capturing sustained regressions.

3) Cure period: legal is comfortable with a 14-day cure period before financial remedies are applied. During those 14 days we will prioritize mitigation and provide daily status updates to EdgeWare. If root cause analysis shows immediate remediation steps that prevent recurrence, we can agree to waive the remedy on a case-by-case basis.

4) Remedy scaling tweak: to address your burst sensitivity, we propose splitting the 2.0% band into two sub-bands so marginal drops don't jump to a 2% step immediately. New ladder (illustrative):
   - 99.9 — 99.8: 0.5% credit
   - 99.8 — 99.5: 1.25% credit
   - 99.5 — 99.0: 2.0% credit
   - <99.0: 6.0% credit cap

Action items: Ben — can you confirm whether revenue ops needs any extra metadata for the holdback option? Laura — I'll work with you on an exhibit for the 14-day cure and the measurement definition. Marissa — let us confirm the metric pipeline for p99 per-region and the tooling to publish postmortems. Sanjay — if that sounds reasonable we'll prepare a short contract exhibit and a DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Naomi

Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Resilience thresholds and remedy scaling — initial proposal

Naomi, Ben, Marissa, Laura —

Appreciate the thoughtful revisions. Procurement and platform reviewed internally and are aligned on the following: 

- We accept the revised remedy ladder and the regional 99.9 baseline for us-west with the sub-band split you proposed.
- EdgeWare will elect the quarterly holdback mechanism rather than immediate credits; please include the reconciliation cadence and reporting fields (monthly invoice id, remedy amount, applied quarter).
- We request the 14-day cure period be explicit in the exhibit. If Redwood wants to waive remedies based on rapid remediation, please list the criteria (e.g., mitigation deployed, postmortem submitted within 10 business days).

If you can produce a short exhibit with those points, we can route for signatures. We prefer DocuSign and would like to see the exhibit by end of week.

Thanks — let's get this into contract.

Best,
Sanjay
